title: Align invoice finalization window with late-rate-limit retention policy
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Issue: invoices that finalize near hourly boundaries sometimes omit late-arriving rate-limit credits because the billing export job closes invoice batches before the retention window used by the rate-limit credit aggregator completes. Symptoms: customers report unexpectedly large invoices followed by manual refunds; internal audit flags missing credit lines for high-traffic tenants. Root cause hypothesis: the export finalizer snapshots usage windows at invoice close time and does not consult the late-credit retention buffer. The buffer (configured at X minutes) is used by the rate-limit crediter to hold potential credit events, but finalizer uses a shorter cutoff when materializing invoice lines, causing race conditions and lost credit lines when late events are applied after finalization. Goal: ensure deterministic, idempotent invoice generation that accounts for the rate-limit retention buffer and produces a reproducible audit trail for any post-finalization adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: Invoice finalizer includes late-credit buffer: invoices finalized at T will include or reserve state for any rate-limit credits retained until T + retention_window
Exported invoice manifests include a credit-watermark and checksum to allow downstream NetSuite/Stripe mapping and reconcileability
No customer-facing refunds are required for incidents where late-rate-limit credits are within retention_window; instead a reconciliation adjustment line is produced and exported
End-to-end integration test that simulates late meter pulses and validates deterministic invoice lines and idempotent replays
Migration/backfill plan for invoices potentially impacted over the past 30 days
implementation_notes: Plan: 1) introduce explicit credit-watermark in export manifest and persist it in the invoice ledger; 2) change finalizer to consult the rate-limit credit retention service (or extend cutoff) when deciding whether to close an invoice bucket; 3) add an 'adjustment' export path for post-finalization late credits that mirrors primary export schema and keeps idempotency keys; 4) update NetSuite/Stripe mapping to accept adjustment lines and avoid double-charging; 5) provide a backfill runner to replay affected windows using the new watermark semantics.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: extending finalization window increases latency for invoice availability — Mitigation: configurable per-plan finalization policy and opt-in quicker-close for self-serve customers
Risk: missing idempotency in adjustment exports may create duplicate lines — Mitigation: export-level seqnums + manifest checksums and a graceful dedupe in the export applier
Risk: large backfill could overload billing exports — Mitigation: rate-limited backfill with canary tenants and monitoring, plus a kill-switch and tickets for manual intervention
testing_plan: Unit tests for watermark propagation; integration test harness that emits meter events at controlled offsets (on-time, 30s late, 10m late) and validates final invoice lines; shadow run against export staging to assert NetSuite/Stripe mapping for adjustment lines; GA smoke test with a small set of tenants; run backfill on staging and validate invoice parity before running in prod.
deployment_plan: 1) deploy finalizer change behind feature flag; 2) enable flag for internal/test tenants and run 24h shadow exports; 3) enable for 5% of tenants with monitoring alerts for export anomalies; 4) roll to 100% once stable. Backfill to be scheduled during low-traffic window and monitored via billing-export dashboard.
rollback_plan: Flip feature flag to revert to old finalizer semantics. If duplicates appear in exports, mark affected exports as quarantined and run repair job using prior snapshots and dedupe keys.
